message.content:
Driving from San Francisco to Los Angeles along the I‑5 corridor covers roughly **380–400 miles** (about 610–640 km). Under normal conditions—steady traffic, no major detours, and staying within speed limits—the trip typically takes **around 6 to 7 hours**.

**Things that can affect the actual drive time:**

| Factor | Impact on Time |
|--------|----------------|
| **Traffic congestion** (especially near the Bay Area, Sacramento, or the Los Angeles metro area) | Adds 30 min–2 hrs |
| **Roadwork / construction** | Can add 15 min–1 hr per segment |
| **Weather** (fog, rain, or storms) | May slow speeds, especially near the coast |
| **Stops** (fuel, food, rest) | Add 15 min–30 min per stop |
| **Speed limits** (I‑5 is usually 65–75 mph, but can drop to 55 mph in urban areas) | Determines baseline pace |

If you’re planning a trip, it’s a good idea to check real‑time traffic updates (Google Maps, Waze, or local traffic reports) before you leave and during the drive. That way you can adjust your departure time or route to avoid the worst congestion.
